summary: Suggests a straightforward convention for defining traps, the alerts that devices send unprompted, for use with SNMP. It is informational.

eli5.summary: When a device has a problem it can shout for help. This is a way to describe each kind of shout.

questions: what are the standard snmp traps
subtitle: A macro for writing down SNMP traps in MIB modules, offered for information and with a strong warning against new traps.

tldr.problem: The Internet-standard SMI had no way to define traps, the unsolicited alerts an SNMP agent sends, so experimental MIBs that needed their own traps had no convenient notation.
tldr.mechanism: The memo suggests a TRAP-TYPE macro with ENTERPRISE, VARIABLES, DESCRIPTION and REFERENCE clauses, and says how each clause fills in the fields of the SNMP Trap-PDU.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational memo, not a standard. It stresses that traps are strongly discouraged and that the macro is for concise definitions of existing traps, not for creating new ones.

facts.label: Max message size for standard traps

today: RFC 1215 is an Informational memo from March 1991. It does not specify a standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Traps Needed a Convention
sections.content:
The memo opens with history. RFC 1052 described a two-prong plan: use the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP, RFC 1067) in the short term and examine the OSI management framework in the long term. Two documents defined the management information: the Structure of Management Information (SMI) and the Management Information Base (MIB).

Later, RFC 1109 reported that the needs of the SNMP and OSI frameworks differed more than expected, so the requirement that the SMI and MIB work with both was suspended. In May 1990 the core documents became "Standard Protocols" with "Recommended" status: RFC 1155 (how managed objects are defined), RFC 1156 (the MIB) and RFC 1157 (the protocol).
sections.eli5: People first hoped one set of rules would work for two different network systems. It turned out the two were too different, so the SNMP side carried on by itself.

sections.title: The Missing Piece and a Warning
sections.content:
Because the SMI was meant to be protocol-independent, it does not provide a way to define traps. The SNMP itself defines a few standardized traps and lets management enterprises send enterprise-specific traps. Experimental MIBs, however, began to need experiment-specific traps, so a convenient notation was wanted. The memo suggests the TRAP-TYPE macro for this.

The memo says the use of traps is STRONGLY discouraged in the Internet-standard Network Management Framework. The macro is meant to allow concise definitions of existing traps, not to spur the definition of new ones.
sections.eli5: There was no tidy way to describe a gadget's shout for help, so this memo offers one. But it also says: please try not to shout too often.

sections.title: The TRAP-TYPE Macro
sections.content:
A trap definition names an ENTERPRISE (an object identifier) and may add three optional parts. VARIABLES lists MIB objects, DESCRIPTION gives a textual definition and REFERENCE points to a trap, event or alarm defined in another MIB module. The value of the macro is an integer.

The memo notes that the macro expands conceptually at implementation time, not at run time. Its text for the REFERENCE clause says it is useful when de-osifying a MIB produced by some other organization.
sections.eli5: It is a fill-in-the-blanks form: whose trap is it, what extra facts come with it, and what does it mean.

sections.title: How Clauses Fill the Trap-PDU
sections.content:
The ENTERPRISE clause is required. Its value goes into the enterprise field of the SNMP Trap-PDU. The VARIABLES clause gives an ordered list of MIB objects that go, in order, into the variable-bindings field. An agent may add more variables after them.

The macro value is the integer that the registration authority named in the ENTERPRISE clause assigned to the trap. It goes in the specific-trap field, and the generic-trap field is set to enterpriseSpecific(6). The DESCRIPTION clause must be present when the MIB module has no textual description of the trap elsewhere.

Special case: if ENTERPRISE is snmp ({ mib-2 11 }), the value of sysObjectID goes in the enterprise field, the macro value goes in the generic-trap field and the specific-trap field is set to 0. Extra variables must not push the serialized SNMP message past 484 octets. This only lets the macro describe existing standard traps; it does not define new standard ones.
sections.eli5: Each blank on the form goes into a matching slot on the alert message. There is one special rule so the old, built-in alerts can be written with the same form.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The first example is an enterprise-specific myLinkDown trap, defined under { enterprises 9999 }, which carries ifIndex and has the value 2. It signals a failure in one of the communications links in the agent's configuration.

The second shows how the standard traps could be written: coldStart (0), warmStart (1), linkDown (2), linkUp (3), authenticationFailure (4) and egpNeighborLoss (5). The authentication failure description says implementations must be able to generate it and also able to suppress it through an implementation-specific mechanism.
sections.eli5: The memo fills in the form twice: once for a made-up company's broken-link alert, and once for the six alerts every SNMP device already knows.

viz.caption: STANDARD SNMP TRAPS AS WRITTEN WITH TRAP-TYPE (RFC 1215)

items.label: coldStart
items.desc: Sender is reinitializing; configuration or implementation may change.

items.label: warmStart
items.desc: Sender is reinitializing; neither configuration nor implementation changes.

items.label: linkDown
items.desc: A communication link failure was recognized.

items.label: linkUp
items.desc: A communication link has come up.

items.label: authenticationFailure
items.desc: A protocol message was not properly authenticated.

items.label: egpNeighborLoss
items.desc: An EGP neighbor was marked down.
